from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Redundancy: Linear Dependence", ["Redundant vectors add no new reach.", "They lie on the same line.", "This redundancy is linear dependence."])
        
        # Vectors setup
        v1 = Vector([0, 1.5, 0], color=BLUE)
        v2 = Vector([1.5, 0, 0], color=GREEN)
        v3 = Vector([1.5, 1.5, 0], color=YELLOW)
        
        # B019: Use segments
        # Row A-C for vectors (1.5 units)
        self.place_in_area(v1, 'A2', 'C2')
        self.place_in_area(v2, 'A2', 'C2')
        self.place_in_area(v3, 'A2', 'C2')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE), Create(v1), Create(v2), Create(v3))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # v3 is redundant (sum of v1 + v2)
        v3_dashed = DashedLine(start=ORIGIN, end=v3.get_end(), color=YELLOW)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN), Transform(v3, v3_dashed))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        label = Text("Redundant", color="#FF33A8", font_size=24)
        # B011: Tethering
        self.add(label)
        label.next_to(v3, UP)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF33A8"), Write(label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Basis is the minimal spanning set.", "It removes all redundant information.", "Unique coordinates define every space point."]
        self.setup_layout("Efficiency: The Basis", lecture_lines)
        self.lecture.set_opacity(0)
        
        # Animation
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        v1 = Vector([1, 1], color=BLUE)
        v2 = Vector([1, -0.5], color=GREEN)
        basis = VGroup(v1, v2)
        label_v1 = MathTex(r"\mathbf{v}_1", color=BLUE).next_to(v1.get_end(), UP)
        label_v2 = MathTex(r"\mathbf{v}_2", color=GREEN).next_to(v2.get_end(), DOWN)
        basis_group = VGroup(basis, label_v1, label_v2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(self.place_in_area(basis_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_opacity(1)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.3})

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Summary", ["Span defines our reach.", "Independence ensures efficiency.", "Basis is the space's DNA."])
        
        # Prepare visual elements
        span_obj = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.5, color=BLUE), Text("Span", font_size=24)).arrange(DOWN)
        ind_obj = VGroup(Square(side_length=0.8, color=GREEN), Text("Independence", font_size=24)).arrange(DOWN)
        basis_obj = VGroup(Triangle(color=YELLOW), Text("Basis", font_size=24)).arrange(DOWN)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(span_obj), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(span_obj, 'B2', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(ind_obj), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_at_grid(ind_obj, 'B5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(basis_obj), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.place_in_area(basis_obj, 'E2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Concluding text
        final_text = Text("Linear Algebra Foundation", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.play(FadeOut(span_obj), FadeOut(ind_obj), FadeOut(basis_obj))
        self.play(Write(final_text))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Foundations of Linear Algebra: From Combinations to Bases

sections.title: The Ingredients: Linear Combinations and Span
sections.content: Define a linear combination as scaling and adding vectors. Explain 'Span' as the set of all possible reach points in space. Use a 2D plane animation where two vectors 'stretch' their reach across the entire surface.
sections.example: Imagine a robot arm moving in a 2D plane: if you have two motors (vectors), any point the arm can touch is the 'Span'.

sections.title: Redundancy: Linear Dependence
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Linear Dependence' as redundant information. Visually demonstrate two vectors lying on the same line or three vectors forming a flat plane in 3D space, showing that one vector adds no new 'reach'.
sections.example: If you have two GPS satellites (vectors) that are perfectly aligned, the second one provides no new triangulation data—it is 'linearly dependent'.

sections.title: Efficiency: The Basis
sections.content: Define a 'Basis' as the minimal set of vectors that can span the space without any redundancy (linearly independent). Emphasize that every vector in the space can be uniquely represented by a basis.
sections.example: Think of coordinates (x, y) on a map: the basis vectors are North and East. You don't need a third direction to reach any point on the map, and you can't reach all points with just one.

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
sections.content: Recap how Span provides the reach, Independence ensures efficiency, and Basis combines both to form the 'DNA' of a vector space. Connect these to higher-dimensional applications.
sections.example: A video game designer using a 3D coordinate system (basis) to render a character's movement within a 3D environment.
